notes: Searched one to two queries per country, fetching only URLs returned by search. FOUND (7 records): MMR, BLZ, SYC, HTI, SDN, DNK, ARM. RULED OUT / EVIDENCE STOPPED: ABW - searched Centrale Bank van Aruba director/integrity; all hits were the Curacao and Sint Maarten central bank (Emsley Tromp, CBCS deputy director forgery), which is CUW/SXM, not Aruba; nothing on CBA itself. BHR - searched Central Bank of Bahrain employee/official court verdicts; all hits were CBB enforcing against Future Bank and Bank Markazi (Iran) or unrelated public-sector bribery; CBB appears only as regulator. BHS - searched Central Bank of The Bahamas employee fraud/court; hits were commercial bank tellers, BPL and Ministry of Finance staff; nothing naming CBOB staff. BRB - searched Central Bank of Barbados plus auditor general; only a press release about an 'incident on its premises', a scam-video warning and Audit Office reports on government accounts; no finding against the bank. BMU - searched Bermuda Monetary Authority plus auditor general and commission of inquiry; auditor general and 2017 COI findings concern government ministries and Port Royal/Bermuda Housing, not the BMA. BRN - searched Brunei Darussalam Central Bank official corruption; hits were Brunei judges, immigration officers and the Ramzidah/Nabil case, none at the central bank (AMBD/BDCB). CAN - searched Bank of Canada employee charged fraud/breach of trust; every hit was a Royal Bank of Canada employee (the Carney data case), not the central bank. COM - searched Banque Centrale des Comores detournement/condamne in French; hits were the Union des MECK microfinance network, an airports director and a Guinea central bank governor; nothing at the BCC. CPV - searched Banco de Cabo Verde plus Tribunal de Contas; hits were Cabo Verde's PGR audit of the presidency and Portuguese Tribunal de Contas work on Novo Banco; nothing on the BCV. DJI and WSM - combined search of Central Bank of Djibouti and Central Bank of Samoa plus governor/corruption/audit; only CBS annual reports, audited financial statements and the CBS Act; no adverse finding. EGY - two searches (English ACA-focused and Arabic 'al-bank al-markazi al-masri' bribery/court); all results were other Egyptian bodies (customs, Alexandria deputy governor, EGOTH, State Council); nothing naming CBE staff or the bank as subject. ERI - no credible published source found and no search returned anything about the Bank of Eritrea; no reporting or audit material located. FJI - searched Reserve Bank of Fiji plus auditor general/FICAC; hits were FICAC and audit work on FRA, Rewa Dairy, Fiji Daily Post and the ADB meeting, plus RBF's own financial-intelligence reporting (the bank enforcing); the parliament page https://www.parliament.gov.fj/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Appendices_RBF_2021-2024.pdf (RBF 2021-2024 appendices tabled in Parliament) was not opened and NEEDS A HAND CHECK for audit qualifications or internal-control findings. OMN - searched Central Bank of Oman employee embezzlement/court; hits were Oman Arab Bank, Ministry of Education and Oman Oil cases; nothing at the CBO. PSE - searched Palestine Monetary Authority plus Anti-Corruption Commission; AMAN integrity reports and PACC coverage name PA ministries and the settlements commissioner, and PMA appears only as an MoU signatory on AML work; nothing with the PMA as subject. QAT - searched Qatar Central Bank official corruption/convicted; the big case is former finance minister Ali Shareef al-Emadi (20 years, money laundering), a ministry not the QCB; also Hamad Medical Corporation; nothing at the QCB. SAU - searched SAMA plus Nazaha arrests; Nazaha's published batches name defence, health, interior and municipal staff in the results seen; no release seen naming a Saudi Central Bank employee. SGP - searched MAS officer charged/corruption; every hit was MAS enforcing (Hyflux, prohibition orders, moneychanger work) or CPIB cases at other agencies; nothing with an MAS officer as subject. SLV - searched Banco Central de Reserva plus Corte de Cuentas in Spanish; hits were BANDESAL's ex-president, the ex-first lady's case and a union complaint about the Corte de Cuentas itself; nothing at the BCR. TLS - searched Banco Central de Timor-Leste plus CAC; only BCTL's own FIU pages, statutes and CAC strategy documents; no case naming BCTL. UZB - two searches (Central Bank of Uzbekistan official bribery, and employee embezzlement); all hits were commercial banks (NBU, Xalq Banki, Microcreditbank) or a fake 'pseudo-employee of the Central Bank' impersonation case, which is an outsider defrauding people in the bank's name and was excluded. DENMARK CAVEAT: Rigsrevisionen's report 15/2021 states that it does not audit Danmarks Nationalbank in its central-bank capacity; the record below is filed because the bond issuance was proposed and executed by Nationalbanken and the undocumented expansion wishes were the bank's, while the 'very unsatisfactory' criticism is directed at the Ministry of Finance. The Danish-language whistleblower story at https://www.altinget.dk/hovedstaden/artikel/det-startede-med-en-mail-fra-en-whistleblower-nu-kan-et-telefonopkald-fra-nationalbanken-blive-en-sag-for-fn (a phone call from Nationalbanken possibly becoming a UN matter) is paywalled and NEEDS A HAND CHECK.

records.people: Bo Bo Nge (deputy governor, Central Bank of Myanmar)
records.summary: Bo Bo Nge, appointed deputy governor of the Central Bank of Myanmar in 2017 under the National League for Democracy government, was detained after the 2021 coup and sentenced by a junta court in December 2022 to 20 years in prison on a corruption charge over what the court called mismanagement of banks trading foreign currency.
records.source_title: Myanmar junta sentences former Central Bank official to 20 years in prison

records.category: political interference in central bank leadership
records.people: Manuel Gustavo Vasquez (governor, Central Bank of Belize)
records.summary: Central Bank of Belize governor Manuel Gustavo Vasquez left office in August 2021 after what media reports described as a dispute with the prime minister over the bank's integrity and operational autonomy; the bank announced his departure on 13 August without giving a reason, and the former governor said he was forced out after a conflict over special interests.
records.source_title: Belizean governor fired by prime minister after 'integrity' row - reports

records.people: Pierre Laporte (former governor, Central Bank of Seychelles)
records.summary: Pierre Laporte, who left the governorship of the Central Bank of Seychelles in March 2012 to become finance minister, was accused in an anonymous letter circulated in September 2012 of drawing two salaries at the same time, one from the central bank and one from the government; he denied wrongdoing and said he had negotiated a severance package to offset the lower ministerial pay.
records.source_title: Former Seychelles governor denies drawing double wage

records.people: Venel Joseph (former governor, Banque de la Republique d'Haiti)
records.summary: Venel Joseph, former governor of Haiti's central bank, was barred from leaving the country in April 2004 by justice minister Bernard Gousse, who named him among 37 former officials to be kept available for investigations into crimes allegedly committed by the government of ousted president Jean-Bertrand Aristide; the minister called the travel ban an insurance policy.
records.source_title: Ex-cb chief banned from leaving Haiti

records.summary: A 2021 investigation by The Sentry found that banking supervision by the Central Bank of Sudan remains weak despite repeated promises of improvement by its leaders, that the bank's capacity to crack down on corruption is largely untested, and that it should be subject to forensic audits by an international body and confirm the sale of all its shareholdings in commercial banks.
records.source_title: Sudan Banking Reforms: Lessons and Recommendations (The Sentry, October 2021)

records.people: Danmarks Nationalbank (state debt manager); Ministry of Finance
records.summary: Rigsrevisionen's report 15/2021, published in 2022, examined the 30-year Danish government bond that Danmarks Nationalbank issued as state debt manager from 2008, totalling DKK 87.6bn; the auditors found no documentation of the bank's wishes behind the expansion of the issue beyond DKK 80bn, and the Public Accounts Committee called the justification for DKK 27.6bn of it very unsatisfactory and said it had caused the state higher interest costs than necessary.
records.source_title: Beretning 15/2021 om Finansministeriets udstedelse af 30-arige statsobligationer i 2008 (Rigsrevisionen)

records.category: conflict of interest in ownership of a commercial bank
records.people: Maneh Tandilyan (former labour minister, accuser); Tigran Avinyan (former deputy prime minister, Armbusinessbank board)
records.summary: In February 2022 Armbusinessbank's new ownership was registered as MFM Global Invest LLC of Switzerland with 74.998% and Housing for Young Families, a refinancing credit organisation founded by the Central Bank of Armenia, with 25.001%; former labour minister Maneh Tandilyan publicly called the deal non-transparent and a gross violation of the law barring the regulator from interfering in commercial banks' activities, and the central bank gave no comment to the news agency.
records.source_title: 'Mysterious' deal in Armenian banking sector or how Central Bank became shareholder of commercial bank
